I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. I am in Quzhou, on the North China Plain, and for me the safest way to make money and keep the land working hard is winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. I do not want to spread myself across too many crops, because I only have primary schooling and I prefer a system I know well, can manage on time, and can sell easily. Wheat gives me a steady grain crop through spring and early summer, and maize follows right after harvest and uses the summer heat and rain. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, put most fertilizer into nitrogen but still keep some phosphorus and potassium so the crop does not weaken, irrigate wheat more than maize because spring is often dry, and stay alert for weeds, aphids, rust, armyworm, and corn borers. For tillage, I will rotary till before wheat, then I will mostly go with no-tillage or very light handling after wheat harvest so I can sow maize fast and keep moisture. That is the plan I would trust most for one full year.
